.. changelog::
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 1.4.26
   ```
   :released: October 19, 2021

    .. change::
        :tags: orm
        :tickets: 6284

        Passing a :class:`.Query` object to :meth:`_orm.Session.execute` is not
        the intended use of this object, and will now raise a deprecation warning.

    .. change::
        :tags: bug, postgresql
        :tickets: 5387

        Added a "disconnect" condition for the "SSL SYSCALL error: Bad address"
        error message as reported by psycopg2. Pull request courtesy Zeke Brechtel.

    .. change::
        :tags: bug, orm

        Improved the exception message generated when configuring a mapping with
        joined table inheritance where the two tables either have no foreign key
        relationships set up, or where they have multiple foreign key relationships
        set up. The message is now ORM specific and includes context that the
        :paramref:`_orm.Mapper.inherit_condition` parameter may be needed
        particularly for the ambiguous foreign keys case.


    .. change::
        :tags: bug, sql
        :tickets: 6520

        Fixed issue where SQL queries using the
        :meth:`_functions.FunctionElement.within_group` construct could not be
        pickled, typically when using the ``sqlalchemy.ext.serializer`` extension
        but also for general generic pickling.

    .. change::
        :tags: bug, orm
        :tickets: 7189

        Fixed issue with :func:`_orm.with_loader_criteria` feature where ON
        criteria would not be added to a JOIN for a query of the form
        ``select(A).join(B)``, stating a target while making use of an implicit
        ON clause.

    .. change::
        :tags: bug, orm
        :tickets: 7205

        Fixed bug where the ORM "plugin", necessary for features such as
        :func:`_orm.with_loader_criteria` to work correctly, would not be applied
        to a :func:`_sql.select` which queried from an ORM column expression if it
        made use of the :meth:`_sql.ColumnElement.label` modifier.



    .. change::
        :tags: bug, mypy
        :tickets: 6435

        Fixed issue in mypy plugin to improve upon some issues detecting ``Enum()``
        SQL types containing custom Python enumeration classes. Pull request
        courtesy Hiroshi Ogawa.

    .. change::
        :tags: bug, mysql
        :tickets: 7144

        Fixed issue in MySQL :func:`_mysql.match` construct where passing a clause
        expression such as :func:`_sql.bindparam` or other SQL expression for the
        "against" parameter would fail. Pull request courtesy Anton Kovalevich.


    .. change::
        :tags: bug, mssql
        :tickets: 7160

        Fixed issue with :meth:`.Inspector.get_foreign_keys` where foreign
        keys were omitted if they were established against a unique
        index instead of a unique constraint.


    .. change::
        :tags: usecase, mssql

        Added reflection support for SQL Server foreign key options, including
        "ON UPDATE" and "ON DELETE" values of "CASCADE" and "SET NULL".

    .. change::
        :tags: bug, sql
        :tickets: 4123

        Repaired issue in new :paramref:`_sql.HasCTE.cte.nesting` parameter
        introduced with :ticket:`4123` where a recursive :class:`_sql.CTE` using
        :paramref:`_sql.HasCTE.cte.recursive` in typical conjunction with UNION
        would not compile correctly.  Additionally makes some adjustments so that
        the :class:`_sql.CTE` construct creates a correct cache key.
        Pull request courtesy Eric Masseran.

    .. change::
        :tags: bug, engine
        :tickets: 7130

        Fixed issue where the deprecation warning for the :class:`.URL` constructor
        which indicates that the :meth:`.URL.create` method should be used would
        not emit if a full positional argument list of seven arguments were passed;
        additionally, validation of URL arguments will now occur if the constructor
        is called in this way, which was being skipped previously.

    .. change::
        :tags: bug, orm
        :tickets: 7103

        Add missing methods added in :ticket:`6991` to
        :class:`_scoping.scoped_session` and :func:`_asyncio.async_scoped_session`.

    .. change::
        :tags: bug, examples
        :tickets: 7169

        Repaired the examples in examples/versioned_rows to use SQLAlchemy 1.4 APIs
        correctly; these examples had been missed when API changes like removing
        "passive" from :meth:`_orm.Session.is_modified` were made as well as the
        :meth:`_ormevents.SessionEvents.do_orm_execute()` event hook were added.

    .. change::
        :tags: bug, orm
        :tickets: 6974, 6972

        An extra layer of warning messages

author: gcbsumid
body:
In order to account for possible slippage in orders, we include a "Max Spend" in the FillBuyOrder or FillSellOrder functions.

If an FillBuy/SellOrder transaction has orders that have been filled before the transaction is able to finish, it may end up slipping and increasing the amount of tokens spent. 

Order 1 - $10 for 3 assets
Order 2 - $20 for 3 assets

Fill Sell Order - 4 items

Ideally, it fills in 3 items from order 1 and 1 item from order 2 and spend $40. But if Order 1 gets filled before this transaction is executed, it may end up buying more items from Order 2 and spend $60 for 3 items instead.

**Describe problem solved by this pull request**

This should allow simplifying `FlightTaskAuto` in a follow-up because it probably contains:
- deprecated mechanisms which were used in the original long gone `FlightTaskAutoLine` and `FlightTaskAutoLineSmooth`

Emoji ### Emoji Los emoji son divertidos :sparkles:, y pueden ser un poco tontos :stuck_out_tongue_winking_eye:, pero también pueden ser una importante herramienta de comunicación al trabajar con equipos remotos ✅. El tono no se transmite tan claramente cuando leemos texto, si lo comparamos con una conversación cara a cara, y los emojis pueden ser una ayuda a la hora de comunicar contexto y emociones. :heart: Los emoji son más apropiados cuando se usan como extras adicionales, no en sustitución del texto. Con las imágenes, el texto descriptivo (alt-text) ayuda a hacerla más accesibles para lectores de pantalla, pero no está garantizado que los lectores de pantalla sepan transmitir la intencionalidad de un emoji. Asegúrate de que tu significado está claro a través del texto, de manera que los emoji resulten de ayuda en lugar de generar más confusión. Enable a dedicated GitHub Actions step to build the Go binaries:

- uses [Goreleaser](https://goreleaser.com/) similarly to our released binaries
- coverage support: with enable-coverage flag, builds produce a `pulumi` CLI compiled for coverage tracking
- tests download and test the exact same binaries
- builds run in a parallel matrix per platform to speed them up
- macos builds necessarily run on a macos-latest worker because of CGO
- windows builds run on an ubuntu-latest worker with cross-compilation
  
Remaining work will build upon this:

- Refactor Windows builds (not touched with this change) to use the same structure
- Apply the changes to non-PR workflows - release, prerelease, master
- Figure out release integration so during release it's obvious that exact same binaries are tested as being released

Some ideas were attempted but look to require non-trivial changes to the test scripts and will not be done:

- Factor out Python wheel build similarly so it is not rebuilt during testing
- Ditto for Node tarball
- Ditto for Go SDK and test suites (separate from CLI pulumi binary and providers)

author: gzili
body:
- Made `ReservationsService` in `OffersController` lazy loaded to fulfill the lazy loading requirement. While this probably doesn't give any performance benefit for such a simple object, `ReservationsService` is quite a good candidate for lazy loading as theoretically offers are listed more often than they are reserved.
- Made `showExpired` a proper boolean parameter. Saw it used this way in some Microsoft article. This resulted in cleaner controller code. The value defaults to `false` when no parameter is given.
- Added `includeExpired` parameter to `FindAll` method in `OffersService` and extracted conditional statement here. You may argue that both the controller and service parameters should be named the same but I think that they have different semantic meaning. The controller "shows" the data as it sends it to the user while the service method only decides what to include in the list.
- Installed [EFCore.NamingConventions](https://github.com/efcore/EFCore.NamingConventions) package which automagically transforms all table and column names to `snake_case` when `UseSnakeCaseNamingConvention` extension method is called `DbContext` options builder. The database queries do not need quotes anymore. What an awesome package!
- Deleted all weather forecast stuff. I believe it's been here for long enough and we already have enough examples that these weather forecasts no longer provide any value.

Modified disconnecting behavior, such that the player is no longer removed from all servers. Instead, the player is marked as 'Asleep', which puts them in a mode which does not affect voting. The sleeping players vote can still be shown, but it is not necessary that the player votes to show all votes.

*Description of changes:*
Api server creates the audit log file under the parent directory provided in the api-server argument `--audit-log-path`. Api server handles log rotation as well. If the file already exists, api server runs into an error when trying to rename the log file to enable rotation.

Before this change, api-server logs would have the following error message and would not do any log rotation on audit logs.

E1115 19:51:34.586712       1 metrics.go:110] Error in audit plugin 'log' affecting 1 audit events: can't rename log file: rename /var/log/kubernetes/api-audit.log /var/log/kubernetes/api-audit-2021-11-15T19-51-34.586.log: device or resource busy
```

author: infotroph
body:
## Description
Reports released and currently installed versions of all PEcAn packages, along with datasets for historical release versions and a gratuitously overengineered script for updating the datasets at release time.

Critique vigorously, please, and send me back to the drawing board if it's needed. I went ahead will a full version to show the concept, but I think there's room for debate about basic design decisions here: 
* Does this interface make sense?
* Is it storing the right information?
* Will it continue to scale acceptably as we add new releases and packages?
* Is PEcAn.all the right package for it to live in? Adding it there breaks the current conceptual explanation that "`PEcAn.all` is like `tidyverse`: It doesn't contain any code and doesn't export anything, it only makes sure the other packages are available." 
    * [Edit 2021-11-29: I had been under the impression `tidyverse` contained no code of its own, but apparently it too now exports a couple of version-reporter functions. So maybe the analogy holds up OK!]
* How should this be plumbed into the release process so that it stays up to date without undue manual work?


## Motivation and Context
With the move toward making PEcAn packages available on CRAN, it is no longer practical to assume that all package versions get incremented every PEcAn release, so we need a way to match a release of PEcAn to the versions of the packages it contains.

Note also that once this function is available, I think a natural next step will be to adopt the `x.y.z.9000` version convention for the development versions of all packages. That will help ensure you can always tell whether you're running e.g. the actually-released PEcAn.logger 1.8.0, or a development version of it that will eventually become 1.8.1.

author: eric-arellano
body:
There's no reason to support them. The `SingleSourceField` should be 0-1 file, so a glob would cause an error. While it is technically possible to have a glob that only matches one file, that's error-prone.

Enforcing this unblocks us from rendering a useful file name representing the target type in more places without needing to hydrate. For example, our streaming workunit handler code uses `Address.filename`, but that doesn't work with manually created per-file targets like `python_source`: https://github.com/pantsbuild/pants/pull/13627. This PR means that we can instead use `SingleSourceField.file_path` for the same effect.

author: jordanstephens
body:
## What are you trying to accomplish?

I'm trying to solve https://github.com/Shopify/packwerk/issues/103 ([Bug] Packwerk.yml exclude option does not work)

More concretely, I'm trying to enable `packwerk validate` to return a successful exit code on a workspace which looks like this:

```
.
├── package.yml
├── packwerk.yml
├── app
│   └── ...
├── node_modules
│   └── foo
│       └── package.yml
└── packages
   └── bar
        ├── package.yml
        └── ...
```

With a `packwerk.yml` file which looks like this:

```yml
include:
- "{app,packages}/**/*.{rb,rake,erb}"

# List of patterns for folder paths to exclude
exclude:
- "node_modules/**/*"

# Patterns to find package configuration files
package_paths: "{.,packages/**}"
```

Right now, I see the following output:

```
% bin/packwerk validate
📦 Packwerk is running validation...

Validation failed ❗
Expected package paths for all package.ymls to be specified, but paths were missing for the following manifests:

node_modules/foo/package.yml
```

I expected the `exclude` configuration option to exclude files in `node_modules` from being relevant to packwerk, but as discussed in #103, `check_package_manifest_paths` has hardcoded `"**/"` as being the relevant scope for validation and `package_manifests` does not know about the configuration object at all.

```ruby 
    def check_package_manifest_paths
      all_package_manifests = package_manifests("**/")
      package_paths_package_manifests = package_manifests(package_glob)

      difference = all_package_manifests - package_paths_package_manifests

      if difference.empty?
        Result.new(true)
      else
        Result.new(
          false,
          <<~EOS
            Expected package paths for all package.ymls to be specified, but paths were missing for the following manifests:

            #{relative_paths(difference).join("\n")}
          EOS
        )
      end
    end
```
https://github.com/Shopify/packwerk/blob/main/lib/packwerk/application_validator.rb#L200-L218

## What approach did you choose and why?

Following the suggestion made by @exterm in https://github.com/Shopify/packwerk/issues/103#issuecomment-966467443, I have added a third parameter to `PackageSet.package_paths` to allow the `configuration.exclude` list to be passed.

I don't love passing a third parameter here—the API feels awkward. I originally tried to pass the whole `Configuration` object into `PackageSet.package_paths`, but that led to a much much larger diff trying to avoid subtle issues in how `Configuration#root_path` is derived from the `config_path` argument to the `Configuration` constructor. I do think that passing the whole configuration object would be a better route to go ultimately, but I think there are some larger refactorings that should be considered which I think would be best considered in isolation of this bugfix. For example:
* `PackageSet.load_all_from` would have to accept a configuration object rather than a simple path.
* `PackageSet.package_paths` is a strange method which never instantiates a `PackageSet`, as its logic grows more complex, it is starting to feel like it might be better for its logic not to have to be crammed into public `PackageSet` class methods next to unrelated concerns.
* `RunContext` should perhaps just hold a reference to `configuration` rather than its independent properties
* Deriving `Configuration#root_path` via `File.dirname(config_path)` means that you have to be careful about setting the final `/` on any `config_path`. You can see how this plays out in the test diffs in my branch. Where I had to do this to work around it:
```diff
-      packages = ::Packwerk::PackageSet.load_all_from(app_dir)
+      configuration = Configuration.new({}, config_path: "#{app_dir}/.")
+      packages = ::Packwerk::PackageSet.load_all_from(configuration)
```

 If you're curious, you can take a look at my attempt [here](https://github.com/Shopify/packwerk/compare/main...jordanstephens:exclude). I'd be happy to pick that work up again and push it over the finish line if there is an appetite for some refactoring here—just let me know.

## What should reviewers focus on?

Correctness, unintended side effects.

@exterm took a look at the potential performance of using the exclude glob to reject matches [here](https://github.com/Shopify/packwerk/issues/103#issuecomment-966472594) and it sounds like they are not concerned after trying it out on a large codebase.

Note: I have not added any new tests yet to cover the new argument to `PackageSet.package_paths`. Once I get confirmation that this is an acceptable approach for the time-being, I will write some tests.

Thanks!

- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Non-breaking change (a change that doesn't alter functionality - i.e., code refactor, configs, etc.)

We were running into a case where the host would send us a 0 length packet if on a SendObject the file fit exactly in full packets... Then it would send one that said no more data on that file.

Our code did not look in the transfer->status field to extract the count transferred.
The code now extracts that and only copies that many bytes and returns it to caller.

This helps clear up some of the issues and crashes we have been seeing. 

I am assuming you would prefer the simple fix here and not go off my other branch which added in support
for RawHid512... Although the tests using it were sort of nice as with it you do get 8 times the data throughput

author: sam-heilbron
body:
# Description

Refactor some code to make it easier to implement a new HybridGateway type, where multiple FilterChains can be explicitly configured by users.

# Context

We are in the process of extending the API to enable a single Gloo Listener to configure multiple filter chains. To enable that, our Gateway resource (that is translated into a Gloo Listener) will support a TcpGateway (it already does), HttpGateway (it alreayd does) and a new HybridGateway (not yet added), which will be a list of Tcp or Http gateways. 

Our translation loop currently makes the assumption that a Gloo Listener will have a single instance of either a TcpGateway or an HttpGateway. To support the new API, we will need to change all the code that currently make that assumption.

This is Part 1 of this change. The goal was to make a non-functional change, keeping our existing tests, and introduce an abstraction (https://martinfowler.com/bliki/BranchByAbstraction.html) that we can implement for our new Gateway type. 

### What's the approach?
This attempts to follow the Dependency Inversion Principle:
```
High-level modules should not depend on low-level modules. Both should depend on abstractions.
Abstractions should not depend on details. Details should depend on abstractions.
```

In our code, we handle TcpLIsteners and HttpListeners in most of the same code, and each function handles the branching logic itself. This makes it challenging to track which code is actually responsible for generating TcpListeners and which is used for HttpListeners. To enable this, we make our translation loop depend on abstractions and instantiate separate code paths for http and tcp support.

An HttpListener needs:
- A way to create its RouteConfiguration
- A way to create an HttpFilterChain

A TcpListener needs:
- A way to create a TcpFilterChain

### This is a big PR, how do we know it is safe?
All changes are contained within the translatorInstance (https://github.com/solo-io/gloo/blob/master/projects/gloo/pkg/translator/translator.go#L86) and we have unit tests for this instance. We've changed the implementation of that translator (introducing sub-translators which have more focused responsibilities). If all the existing tests pass, I'm comfortable we didn't break anything.

### What code changed?
Largely this PR copied/pasted code. By creating actual instances of translators, the main differences are just that some instances that were previously passed as arguments in functions are now struct variables. 

There we a couple of small changes: 
1. We used to call `routeConfigName()` deep down in the translation loop. Now I do it at constructor time and pass in the value, ensuring that the value is the same for the RouteConfig and Listener.
2. We used to determine if the VirutalHosts required Tls by checking the SslConfiguration lenght. Similar to above, we inject the dependencies instead of handling that logic in the translation loop. We rely on the same function. The purpose of this change is that when we support a HybridGateway, the determination for whether or not to require Tls on VirtualHosts will be different.

### What comes next?
This first pass tries to create a clear abstraction that the new gateway type could implement. Next, I'd like to write tests around the sub-translators. Then, I'd like to change the interface of plugins so that instead of receiving a top-level listener, they receive only the parameters they really need (either a TcpListener or HttpListener). This way, we can run the translation loop N times, for N instances of either a TcpListener or HttpListener on our new hybrid gateway type.


# Checklist:

- [x] I included a concise, user-facing changelog (for details, see https://github.com/solo-io/go-utils/tree/master/changelogutils) which references the issue that is resolved.
- [ ] If I updated APIs (our protos) or helm values, I ran `make -B install-go-tools generated-code` to ensure there will be no code diff
- [x] I followed guidelines laid out in the Gloo Edge [contribution guide](https://docs.solo.io/gloo-edge/latest/contributing/)
- [x] I opened a draft PR or added the work in progress label if my PR is not ready for review

author: 0o-de-lally
body:
Issue: Users trying to onboard other users without having mined.

If your balance is below 1 gas, you can’t onboard people. This will likely happen if you are new to the network, on your first day. The solution is to mine, and wait until next epoch, then you’ll have enough to onboard many others others.

This is not well explained in documentation. Patching it here.

author: kommiharibabu
body:
Adding a version information flag to identify whether the metadata
have a proper snapshot information or not by comparing the retrieved
version information with the binary version.

With this new flag, all the older versions that don't have this flag
are treated having not proper snapshots and ignored them during rollback
to stable operation.

author: rpiaggio
body:
The previous implementation was flawed and it would yield wrong results when called within a short period of time.

This new implementation fixed the problems by using the Ref+Deferred pattern as a latch, so that new invocations await until the previous one is completely enqueued.
